title: Security of OCB2 with Nonempty Associated Data
summary: All motivating OCB2 attacks rely on empty-associated-data forgeries; determine whether restricting every operation to nonempty associated data, including fixed-prefix enforcement, makes OCB2 secure or admits a counterexample.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether $\mathrm{OCB2}$ is secure when every encryption and decryption operation uses associated data $A \ne \varepsilon$, including the generic variant that enforces this restriction by prepending a fixed nonempty string—such as $\texttt{A}$ or $0^n$—to every associated-data input, even an originally empty input. All $\mathrm{OCB2}$ attacks motivating this question use a forgery with $A=\varepsilon$ as a key component. Prove security under the restriction $A\ne\varepsilon$ or refute it by giving a counterexample attack.

scope.domain: Symmetric authenticated encryption, focused on the OCB2 construction and nonempty associated-data restrictions.
assumptions: Every encryption and decryption operation uses nonempty associated data.
parameters: Associated data: the input whose nonemptiness is restricted
Fixed nonempty prefix: prepended to every associated-data input in the generic enforcement variant, including an originally empty input
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether restricted OCB2 is secure or admits a counterexample attack.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of OCB2: Attacks on Authenticity and Confidentiality

progress.summary: The source notes that a forgery with empty associated data is a key component of all its OCB2 attacks. It presents nonempty associated data, optionally enforced by prepending a fixed string, as a possible fix but does not provide the required security proof.
citation_labels: Akiko Inoue et al., Cryptanalysis of OCB2: Attacks on Authenticity and Confidentiality
